number.why: The source confirms dabigatran versus warfarin HR 1.10 (95% CI 0.65–1.84) for recurrent symptomatic VTE and VTE-related deaths through six months. Agreement is limited to that treatment window and the restricted FAS population; the ruling correctly identifies the served unrestricted ITT label as inaccurate. A longer post-treatment analysis exists and must not be conflated with this estimate.

quotes.span: The primary outcome was the 6-month incidence of recurrent symptomatic, objectively confirmed venous thromboembolism and related deaths.
RESULT OUTCOME 0 ANALYSIS 2: groups Dabigatran 150 mg, Warfarin | Hazard Ratio (HR) 1.10 (95% CI 0.65 to 1.84) | p None | METHOD Regression, Cox | Patients without events are censored at day 180

Full analysis set (FAS): consisted of all randomised patients who were documented to have taken at least one dose of study drug. Patients were assigned to the treatment groups as randomised, i.e. regardless of the actual medication taken.

RESULT OUTCOME 0 ANALYSIS 0: groups Dabigatran 150 mg, Warfarin | Hazard Ratio (HR) 1.05 (95% CI 0.65 to 1.70) | p <0.0001 | METHOD Regression, Cox | Patients without events are censored at the end of post treatment period (day 224)

entry.why: The registry explicitly establishes adults with acute symptomatic VTE receiving dabigatran versus warfarin following initial parenteral anticoagulation. The FAS restriction concerns analysis population, not whether the entry population satisfies the question.

quotes.span: A Phase III, Randomised, Double Blind, Parallel-group Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Oral Dabigatran Etexilate 150 mg Twice Daily Compared to Warfarin (INR 2.0-3.0) for 6 Month Treatment of Acute Symptomatic Venous Thromboembolism (VTE), Following Initial Treatment (5-10 Days) With a Parenteral Anticoagulant Approved for This Indication.

Inclusion criteria 1. Acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT) of the leg involving proximal veins, and/or pulmonary embolism (PE) iin patients for whom at least 6 months of anticoagulant therapy is considered appropriate 2. Male or female, being 18 years of age or older

missed: The ruling omitted the alternative primary-endpoint post-treatment analysis, quoted above from evidence/held/registry/NCT00291330.json: HR 1.05 (95% CI 0.65 to 1.70), censored at day 224. If the served timepoint means longest follow-up including the post-treatment period, that is the relevant estimate; HR 1.10 is confirmed only for the six-month acute-treatment window. This does not change the entry ruling.
